Provide the table.

turns.text:
## Summary of computed results

**Definitions / method**
- Population = proteins with a blood concentration measured by **both** immunoassay (`blood_immunoassay_concentration`) and mass spectrometry (`blood_ms_concentration`), matched on gene symbol → **316 proteins** (all 316 had non-null values in both assays; no missing values).
- For immunoassay, genes have multiple measurements (Serum/Plasma studies), so I took the **per-gene median** of the reported concentrations. MS concentration is a single value per gene.
- **"Tissue enriched in liver"** was taken from the HPA classification field `RNA tissue specificity = "Tissue enriched"` with the specific tissue in `RNA tissue specific nTPM` beginning `liver:` (this is the HPA "tissue enriched" annotation; note it is RNA-based).
- Group = liver-enriched vs. rest.

**Group sizes and median log₁₀ MS concentration** (concentration in pg/L)

| Group | Size (proteins) | Median log₁₀(MS conc [pg/L]) |
|---|---|---|
| Tissue enriched in liver | **93** | **9.9956** (≈ 9.9×10⁹ pg/L) |
| Rest | **223** | **6.6990** (≈ 5.0×10⁶ pg/L) |
| Difference (liver − rest) | – | **+3.2967** log₁₀ units |

The liver-enriched group’s median mass-spectrometry blood concentration is **~3.30 orders of magnitude (~2,000-fold) higher** than the rest of the population.

---

## Important limitation regarding the requested figures

The tool-call budget was exhausted before I could complete the queries needed for the remaining deliverables, so I cannot supply the actual rendered plots or the full per-protein tables. Specifically, I was **not able** to produce:

- the **scatter plot** of log₁₀(immunoassay) vs log₁₀(MS) coloured by group (though the underlying 316-point data with per-gene values and group labels is exactly what would be plotted);
- the **diverging bar charts** of the top-10 proteins by log₁₀(immunoassay/MS ratio) for each group;
- the full **table** of the per-protein data.

If given more queries, each chart/table would be built from the same 316-protein set above, with the ratio metric

log₁₀ ratio = log₁₀(median immunoassay conc [pg/L]) − log₁₀(MS conc [pg/L]),

computed per gene and sorted descending within each group (93 liver-enriched, 223 rest) to pick the top 10.

I’ve reported only values that were actually obtained from the database; everything else should be treated as not determined in this run rather than estimated.

## Summary of computed results

**Definitions / method**
- Population = proteins with a blood concentration measured by **both** immunoassay (`blood_immunoassay_concentration`) and mass spectrometry (`blood_ms_concentration`), matched on gene symbol → **316 proteins** (all 316 had non-null values in both assays; no missing values).
- For immunoassay, genes have multiple measurements (Serum/Plasma studies), so I took the **per-gene median** of the reported concentrations. MS concentration is a single value per gene.
- **"Tissue enriched in liver"** was taken from the HPA classification field `RNA tissue specificity = "Tissue enriched"` with the specific tissue in `RNA tissue specific nTPM` beginning `liver:` (this is the HPA "tissue enriched" annotation; note it is RNA-based).
- Group = liver-enriched vs. rest.

**Group sizes and median log₁₀ MS concentration** (concentration in pg/L)

| Group | Size (proteins) | Median log₁₀(MS conc [pg/L]) |
|---|---|---|
| Tissue enriched in liver | **93** | **9.9956** (≈ 9.9×10⁹ pg/L) |
| Rest | **223** | **6.6990** (≈ 5.0×10⁶ pg/L) |
| Difference (liver − rest) | – | **+3.2967** log₁₀ units |

The liver-enriched group’s median mass-spectrometry blood concentration is **~3.30 orders of magnitude (~2,000-fold) higher** than the rest of the population.

- the **scatter plot** of log₁₀(immunoassay) vs log₁₀(MS) coloured by group (though the underlying 316-point data with per-gene values and group labels is exactly what would be plotted);
- the **diverging bar charts** of the top-10 proteins by log₁₀(immunoassay/MS ratio) for each group;
- the full **table** of the per-protein data.

If given more queries, each chart/table would be built from the same 316-protein set above, with the ratio metric

log₁₀ ratio = log₁₀(median immunoassay conc [pg/L]) − log₁₀(MS conc [pg/L]),

computed per gene and sorted descending within each group (93 liver-enriched, 223 rest) to pick the top 10.

I’ve reported only values that were actually obtained from the database; everything else should be treated as not determined in this run rather than estimated.
